turbomachinery.pump_power.title: Pump hydraulic power, shaft power and efficiency

variables.name: P_hyd
variables.desc: hydraulic (fluid) power rho g Q H

assumptions: eta = P_hyd/P_shaft is the overall pump efficiency. H is the total head added to the fluid across the pump.
method_references: P_hyd = rho g Q H; eta = P_hyd/P_shaft

turbomachinery.npsh_available.title: Net positive suction head available (NPSHa)

variables.name: T
variables.desc: liquid temperature at the pump suction

variables.name: p_s
variables.desc: absolute pressure at the free surface

variables.name: z_s
variables.desc: static suction head (positive if the liquid level is above the pump)

variables.name: h_loss
variables.desc: friction + minor loss head in the suction line

variables.name: p_vap
variables.desc: vapour pressure of the liquid at T

procedure.python:
def _npsh_available(values):
    """Net positive suction head available, with vapour pressure from common.saturation."""
    fluid = _fluid_name(values['fluid'])
    T, p_s, z_s, h_loss, rho, g = (values[k] for k in ('T', 'p_s', 'z_s', 'h_loss', 'rho', 'g'))
    sat = common.saturation(fluid, T=T)
    p_vap = sat['P']
    npsh = (p_s - p_vap) / (rho * g) + z_s - h_loss
    return {'NPSH_A': npsh, 'p_vap': p_vap}

assumptions: NPSHa = (p_s - p_vap)/(rho g) + z_s - h_loss. The vapour pressure p_vap is computed from common.saturation (CoolProp) at the liquid temperature T, which must lie in the fluid saturation range. Density rho is entered by the user (a liquid at that state).
method_references: NPSH available = (p_s - p_vap)/(rho g) + z_s - h_loss

turbomachinery.npsh_margin.title: NPSH margin (cavitation check against required NPSH)

variables.name: NPSH_R
variables.desc: NPSH required (pump data from the manufacturer)

assumptions: NPSH_R is a pump characteristic obtained from the manufacturer curve, not computed here. Keep margin > 0 (with a safety allowance) to avoid cavitation.
method_references: NPSH margin = NPSHa - NPSHr

turbomachinery.cavitation_number.title: Cavitation number
assumptions: sigma = (p - p_vap)/(0.5 rho V^2); cavitation is expected as sigma approaches the critical (incipient) value for the geometry. p_vap may be taken from npsh_available or the thermo section.
method_references: Cavitation number (Thoma) sigma = (p - p_vap)/(1/2 rho V^2)

turbomachinery.specific_speed.title: Pump specific speed (dimensionless)

variables.name: omega
variables.desc: angular speed (enter rad/s, rpm or rps)
variables.label: ω

variables.name: Q
variables.desc: flow rate at best efficiency point

variables.name: H
variables.desc: head per stage at best efficiency point

assumptions: Dimensionless specific speed: omega in rad/s, Q in m^3/s, H in m. The traditional US value is N_s,US = N_s x 2733 (n in rpm, Q in gpm, H in ft). Low N_s favours centrifugal, high N_s axial impellers.
method_references: Dimensionless specific speed omega sqrt(Q)/(g H)^(3/4)

turbomachinery.suction_specific_speed.title: Suction specific speed (dimensionless)

variables.name: S
variables.desc: suction specific speed omega sqrt(Q)/(g NPSH_R)^(3/4)

variables.name: omega
variables.desc: angular speed (enter rad/s, rpm or rps)
variables.label: ω

variables.name: Q
variables.desc: flow rate at best efficiency point

variables.name: NPSH_R
variables.desc: required NPSH at best efficiency point

turbomachinery.affinity_laws.title: Pump affinity laws / similarity (speed, diameter and density scaling)
assumptions: Geometrically similar machines; efficiency assumed constant. Q ~ N D^3, H ~ N^2 D^2, P ~ rho N^3 D^5. Impeller trimming (cutting D in the same housing) is a separate approximation with slightly different exponents, not this geometric-similarity law.
method_references: Pump affinity laws (Q ~ N D^3, H ~ N^2 D^2, P ~ rho N^3 D^5)

turbomachinery.system_curve.title: System curve (static head plus friction)
assumptions: Quadratic (turbulent) system curve; K lumps pipe friction and minor losses for a given pipe network.
method_references: H_sys = H_static + K Q^2

turbomachinery.operating_point.title: Pump/system operating point (curve intersection)

variables.name: pump_curve
variables.desc: pump head curve [[Q (m^3/s), H (m)], ...] (decreasing H with Q)

assumptions: Linear interpolation of the tabulated pump curve; quadratic system curve. The duty point must lie inside the supplied pump-curve range [Q_min, Q_max]; if the curves cross beyond it the calculator raises rather than extrapolate. For pumps in series add heads at equal Q, in parallel add flows at equal H (see pumps_series_parallel).
method_references: Operating point = intersection of pump and system curves

turbomachinery.pumps_series_parallel.title: Identical pumps in series and parallel

variables.name: H_series
variables.desc: combined head for n pumps in series (same Q)

variables.name: Q_parallel
variables.desc: combined flow for n pumps in parallel (same H)

assumptions: Identical pumps: series adds head at equal flow, parallel adds flow at equal head. The actual combined operating point is the intersection with the system curve (operating_point).
method_references: Series and parallel combination of identical pumps

turbomachinery.euler_turbomachine.title: Euler turbomachine equation (specific work and ideal head)

variables.name: w_euler
variables.desc: specific work (positive = added to the fluid)

variables.name: vu1
variables.desc: tangential component of absolute velocity at inlet

variables.name: vu2
variables.desc: tangential component of absolute velocity at outlet

assumptions: Pump/compressor convention: w > 0 when work is added. Power = mdot * w_euler. For a turbine the fluid does work (w < 0) and the sign is reversed.
method_references: Euler turbomachine equation w = u2 vu2 - u1 vu1

turbomachinery.velocity_triangle.title: Velocity triangle (absolute, relative and blade-speed vectors)

variables.name: alpha
variables.desc: absolute flow angle from the tangential direction
variables.label: α

variables.name: Wu
variables.desc: tangential component of the relative velocity

variables.name: Vu
variables.desc: tangential component of the absolute velocity

variables.name: beta
variables.desc: relative flow angle from the tangential direction
variables.label: β

procedure.python:
def _velocity_triangle(values):
    """Velocity triangle from blade speed U, absolute speed V and absolute flow angle alpha (from tangential)."""
    U, V, alpha = values['U'], values['V'], values['alpha']
    Vu = V * math.cos(alpha)
    Vm = V * math.sin(alpha)
    Wu = Vu - U
    W = math.hypot(Vm, Wu)
    beta = math.atan2(Vm, Wu)
    # Wu is listed first: it depends on all three inputs, so every input is recoverable by inversion.
    return {'Wu': Wu, 'Vm': Vm, 'Vu': Vu, 'W': W, 'beta': beta}

assumptions: V = U + W. Vu = V cos(alpha), Vm = V sin(alpha), Wu = Vu - U, beta = atan2(Vm, Wu). alpha, beta measured from the tangential (U) direction; the angle used in the Euler equation is the tangential component Vu.
method_references: Velocity triangle V = U + W; Vu = V cos(alpha), Vm = V sin(alpha)

turbomachinery.degree_of_reaction.title: Degree of reaction of a turbomachine stage
assumptions: Degree of reaction R = (static enthalpy change across the rotor)/(static enthalpy change across the whole stage). Compressor convention (rotor first): station 1 = rotor inlet, 2 = rotor outlet, 3 = stage (stator) outlet, so R = (h2 - h1)/(h3 - h1). Turbine form (stator first): 1 = stage inlet, 2 = rotor inlet, 3 = rotor outlet, so R = (h2 - h3)/(h1 - h3). An impulse stage has R = 0; an ideal 50% reaction stage has R = 0.5. For an incompressible machine replace h with p/(rho g).
method_references: Degree of reaction R = (h2 - h1)/(h3 - h1) (compressor); R = (h2 - h3)/(h1 - h3) (turbine)

turbomachinery.turbine_power.title: Hydraulic turbine power and efficiency
assumptions: eta is the overall turbine efficiency (P = eta rho g Q H).
method_references: Turbine power P = eta rho g Q H

turbomachinery.turbine_specific_speed.title: Turbine specific speed (dimensionless)

variables.name: omega
variables.desc: angular speed (enter rad/s, rpm or rps)
variables.label: ω

assumptions: Dimensionless turbine specific speed. Impulse (Pelton) machines have low N_s, Francis medium, Kaplan (axial) high; the exact selection ranges are manufacturer data.
method_references: Turbine specific speed omega sqrt(P/rho)/(g H)^(5/4)

turbomachinery.compressor.title: Compressor isentropic work, outlet temperature and efficiency
assumptions: Ideal gas, constant cp and gamma. eta_c = w_s/w_actual, with w_s the isentropic work between the same pressure levels. Real-gas behaviour can be evaluated with the thermo section (common.fluid_state).
method_references: Isentropic compression: T2s = T1 (P2/P1)^((gamma-1)/gamma); w_s = cp (T2s - T1); eta_c = w_s/w_actual

turbomachinery.fan_laws.title: Fan laws (speed scaling for flow, pressure and power)
assumptions: Same fan at different speeds, density unchanged: Q ~ N, dp ~ N^2, P ~ N^3.
method_references: Fan laws (Q ~ N, dp ~ N^2, P ~ N^3)

turbomachinery.fan_total_pressure.title: Fan total pressure from static and velocity pressure
assumptions: Total pressure = static + dynamic (velocity) pressure. The fan total pressure rise is the difference of p_t across the fan.
method_references: p_t = p_s + 1/2 rho V^2

turbomachinery.wind_turbine_power.title: Wind turbine power (power coefficient)
assumptions: Cp is the power coefficient (fraction of the wind power captured); the Betz limit caps Cp at 16/27 ~ 0.593 (see betz_limit).
method_references: P = 1/2 rho A V^3 Cp

turbomachinery.betz_limit.title: Betz limit: maximum extractable wind power
assumptions: Betz (1919) limit: a frictionless actuator disc can extract at most 16/27 of the wind power; no real turbine reaches it.
method_references: Betz limit Cp,max = 16/27 (landmark)

turbomachinery.tip_speed_ratio.title: Tip speed ratio

variables.name: TSR
variables.desc: tip speed ratio omega R / V

variables.name: omega
variables.desc: angular speed (enter rad/s, rpm or rps)
variables.label: ω

assumptions: Tip speed ratio lambda = omega R / V. Modern three-blade turbines peak around lambda ~ 6-8 (design value).
method_references: TSR = omega R / V

turbomachinery.propeller.title: Propeller thrust and efficiency (momentum theory)

variables.name: mdot
variables.desc: mass flow rate through the propeller disc

assumptions: Ideal (actuator-disc) propeller: thrust = momentum change T = mdot (V_e - V_0); propulsive efficiency eta_p = T V_0 / P_shaft. Requires V_e >= V_0.
method_references: Propeller momentum theory: T = mdot (V_e - V_0); eta_p = T V_0 / P_shaft

turbomachinery.froude_efficiency.title: Ideal (Froude) propulsive efficiency
assumptions: Ideal actuator-disc (Froude) propulsive efficiency eta_ideal = 2/(1 + V_e/V_0). Requires V_e >= V_0; static operation (V_0 = 0) gives zero propulsive efficiency.
method_references: Froude propulsive efficiency 2/(1 + V_e/V_0)

turbomachinery.pelton_optimum.title: Pelton wheel optimum bucket speed (u = V/2)
assumptions: For a frictionless Pelton wheel the power is maximised when the bucket speed is half the jet speed, u = V/2; real turbines run slightly below this ideal (u ~ 0.46 V).
method_references: Pelton optimum bucket speed u = V/2 (ideal)
